chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His (peace be upon him) statement 'There is no shuf'ah in animals' is to be understood as referring to the case where there is more than one partner. And we have clarified in what preceded in the narration of Yunus that there is shuf'ah in animals. And to add further clarification, he narrated:

key_terms.الْحَيَوَانِ: Animals (specifically livestock or beasts of burden in this legal context).
key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: Pre-emption, the right of a partner or co-owner to buy out the share of another partner who sells their portion.

ai.seo_question: Does the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) apply to animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s statement that pre-emption (*shuf'ah*) does not apply to animals, which the commentator Muhammad ibn al-Hasan interprets as referring to cases with multiple partners. This ruling is contextualized by reconciling it with other narrations, such as those from Yunus, which affirm the general principle of *shuf'ah* in shared property, thereby demonstrating the Shia scholarly method of harmonizing apparent contradictions through specific contextualization (*ta'wil*).
